input.summary:
P7 east kitchen (parts/room-43.mjs) is furnished: a lit furnace stove at (92,3,15) as the focal piece against the hearth wall, a spruce fence and top-slab counter at (93,3..4,15) with a flower pot, and hanging lanterns at (92,6,14) and (93,6,15). Doorway cell (93,3,14) and the lane to the stove (92,3,14) are kept clear.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt with 7 blocks from this part, no refused writes or off-palette blocks.
On a stand-in shell (walls, floor, y7 ceiling, the hearth campfire, outside gravel) the room check reads OK: 0 dark cells, min light 11, FIT OK.
left: In the real build.nbt the room check still reads UNREACHABLE and the lanterns float, because shell A (walls, floors, y7 ceiling), the lane and the hearth part are still stubs; rerun the check after the merge.

The 2x2 room has no room for a table, chair or bed; the kitchen reads as stove plus counter only. The walker also lists a cell on top of the stove's iron flue plate (92,5,15) as unreached, so the plate may be standable: check after the merge.
plan.md and elements.md have no kitchen-specific checklist item, so nothing was ticked; the kitchen's walls, door and hearth belong to the shell and chimney parts.

waste.what: Checking walkability and light needed a hand-made stand-in shell (walls, floor, y7 ceiling, doorway, hearth campfire, outside ground) written as a throwaway script in /tmp, plus a rooms file with the entrance moved to the door, because the real build has no shell yet.
waste.cost: about 4 retries to get the doorway, outside floor and entrance right; roughly 6 minutes of the 12
waste.tool: mcd room --standin <shell-spec> or a --test-shell option that fills the box's walls, floor, ceiling and doorway from the plan, and an --entrance flag on mcd room so a single room can be checked on its own

waste.what: Working out the layer format of layers() (single layer vs list of layers) by trial: my first attempt nested one array too deep.
waste.tool: a line in the build library doc stating that rowsOrLayers is an array of layers, each an array of row strings; the shape ambiguity bit once

waste.what: Cell-by-cell check that the counter fence and top slab sit at the right heights (fence 1.5 tall, slab top half at y4) and that the stove's flue plate is walkable, done by reasoning rather than a tool.
waste.cost: a few minutes of mental geometry
waste.tool: mcd fit or mcd room could print the standing height of each furniture cell (top of a block or slab, with fence arms) so a counter's surface is read off, not worked out

companions.task: Confirm the two hanging lanterns and the hearth fire through the mouth light every floor cell once the real ceiling and hearth exist, and say whether a candle on the counter would add anything in a room this small.
Build the hearth surround and the stove's brick wall at (92,3,16), which is the chimney part's job, so the stove sits in finished masonry rather than a bare wall cell.
